No fatal findings.

1. `thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation` — [L3] and proof step 2.1 ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation.md:46))

   - What is wrong: [L3] attributes the claim that \(u/\lVert u\rVert\) has norm one to `def-inner-product-norm`.
   - Evidence: the cited [definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-inner-product-norm.md:27) defines
     \(\lVert u\rVert=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle}\), establishes nonnegativity, and explicitly says the norm axioms are proved elsewhere. It does not state the normalization claim.
   - The claim is true and follows immediately by expanding
     \(\langle u/\lVert u\rVert,u/\lVert u\rVert\rangle=1\).
   - Severity: **nonfatal** under the 30-second rule; inaccurate citation/omitted inline derivation.

2. `thm-bessel-inequality-and-finite-parseval-identity` — proof step 3.1 ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-bessel-inequality-and-finite-parseval-identity.md:60))

   - What is wrong: “By [L3],” the proof identifies \(v=p\) exactly with \(v\) belonging to the listed span.
   - Evidence: the cited [lemma](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-span-is-the-set-of-linear-combinations.md:33) states only that the span consists of finite linear combinations. It gives \(p\in\operatorname{span}\{e_i\}\) and therefore \(v=p\Rightarrow v\) lies in the span, but not the reverse for this particular \(p\).
   - The missing reverse bridge is short: if \(v\) lies in the span, then \(v-p\) also lies there; step 1.1 makes \(v-p\) orthogonal to every \(e_i\), hence to itself, so \(v-p=0\).
   - Severity: **nonfatal** under the 30-second rule; unlicensed inference as written.
